solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

blocks.note: to puff is to praise extravagantly, as in a puff piece
what is in is fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher heaps praise on a well-loved seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: The puffin is a stubby, brightly billed bird of North Atlantic cliffs, so seabird is its category.

indicators.note: including means the register takes something inside it, wrapped around the extra piece

blocks.note: a pug is a small flat-faced breed of dog
a register is a list of names
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A kennel club enters one boxer dog on its register.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxer looks like the dog breed next to Dog and register, but it means a fighter in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A pugilist is a formal or jocular word for a prizefighter, someone who boxes.

definitions.note: the answer is a past participle; 'forgotten' here means wilfully overlooked

indicators.note: something that returns goes back the way it came, so this word is read backwards

blocks.note: to forgo is to give up or yield something
nett profit is what is cleared after deductions

explanation.surface: An investment whose clear returns were ignored on purpose by its owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear returns' reads like profits coming back, but returns is the instruction to reverse the word for clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forgotten in this sense has been put out of mind deliberately, left out of consideration.

clue.text: Element of travel sickness around Ely?

definitions.note: definition by example, signalled by the question mark

indicators.note: an element of something is a part of it, so the letters are a run inside the following words
turned around means facing the other way, so the run is read backwards

blocks.note: a run of letters spanning the end of travel and the start of sickness

explanation.surface: Someone feels a bit queasy on the way round Ely.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely in Cambridgeshire was historically the Isle of Ely, raised ground in the Fens, hence the question mark for an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Ely is one instance of an isle, being the old name of the fenland island on which the cathedral city stands.

clue.text: Are incoherent after extremely shambolic emergency take-off

indicators.note: extremely points to the two extremes of the word, its very first and very last letters

blocks.note: the outside letters of the word shambolic
to ramble is to talk incoherently

explanation.surface: Pilots babble in panic after a chaotic emergency take-off.
explanation.walkthrough: After here places the extremes of shambolic before the word for being incoherent.
explanation.definitionFit: A scramble is the urgent launch of fighter aircraft to meet a threat, an emergency take-off.

definitions.note: the answer is the class to which setters belong

indicators.note: with no bounds the word loses its edges, so its first and last letters go

blocks.note: C is the standard symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
the word zaniness with its first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: Crossword setters are endlessly zany, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters looks like the people who compile crosswords; here they are gun dogs, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Setters are a breed of gun dog, and canines is the collective term for dogs.

clue.text: Increase in adjusted per capita income at last

indicators.note: figures that have been adjusted are altered, so these letters are put into a new order
at last points to the final letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: used as written
the last letter of income

explanation.surface: An economist notes a rise in per capita income once figures are adjusted.
explanation.walkthrough: The economics vocabulary makes adjusted look like inflation-adjusted, but it reworks the letters of per capita with the tail of income.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets appreciate when they grow in value, so the verb means to increase.

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter
tailing means following behind, so this piece comes after the colour

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
to rue is to regret, so regretting is ruing

explanation.surface: A black bear briefly regrets following someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Black bear reads as one animal, but black supplies a letter and bear alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruin is a traditional nickname for a bear, from the Dutch for brown, as in folk tales.

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
the verso is the back side of a page

explanation.surface: An English bottom is a frightful sight.
explanation.walkthrough: Backside suggests a bottom; it is the reverse side of a leaf in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever so and frightfully are both intensifying adverbs meaning very, in a rather posh British register.

clue.text: 'Imagine' is almost perfect hit single, ultimately

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word drops its last letter
ultimately means in the end, so the final letters of the next two words are taken

blocks.note: ideal means perfect
the last letters of hit and of single

explanation.surface: John Lennon's Imagine is nearly the perfect hit single.
explanation.walkthrough: The quote marks make 'Imagine' look like the Lennon song title; it is just the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ideate is to form an idea in the mind, which is to imagine or conceive.

indicators.note: rioting suggests disorder and chaos, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: used as written

explanation.surface: A grubby band of rag-and-bone men lead a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: Ragmen are rag-and-bone men, street dealers in old clothes and scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Insalubrious means unhealthy or dirty, and something full of microbes is unwholesome in exactly that way.

blocks.note: p, for piano, is the musical direction meaning quietly
rude means insulting or offensive

explanation.surface: Someone quietly insults a woman called Mrs Grundy.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Grundy is a character from an 18th-century English play whose name became shorthand for a narrow-minded moraliser.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Grundy personifies conventional prudishness, so she stands for someone easily shocked by impropriety.

indicators.note: twisted round means turned to face the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a kitty is a pool of shared money

explanation.surface: A deviant cat has an odd kink.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitty suggests a cat; it is a shared fund of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A kink in a rope or wire is a twist, a small curl or coil in the line.

indicators.note: playing about with letters means moving them round, so these are rearranged

blocks.note: used as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: The revolutionary Lenin was not one for playing games.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawn tennis is the full name of the racket sport, so it is a specific game.

indicators.note: something affected has been altered by an outside influence, so these letters change order

blocks.note: used as written
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A court order has an effect on where someone currently lives.
explanation.walkthrough: Current looks like an adjective meaning present, but it is the physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree nisi was the provisional court ruling in English divorce proceedings, a type of court order.

clue.text: Defiant words from drunk at this point

blocks.note: a sot is a habitual drunk
here means at this place or point

explanation.surface: A drunk shouts defiance at this moment.
explanation.definitionFit: So there is a childish retort of triumph or defiance, a phrase thrown out to end an argument.

indicators.note: harbouring means sheltering inside, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: a spy is a secret agent
Kim Philby was the British intelligence officer who spied for the Soviets

explanation.surface: An agent who sheltered the traitor Philby is exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: Revealing suggests unmasking a mole; here it describes scanty clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A skimpy outfit covers little, so it is revealing in the sense of showing a lot of skin.

clue.text: Training facility in China was essentially established by Gunners

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or core of the word, its central letter

blocks.note: china is rhyming slang for mate, from china plate, and a mate is a pal
the central letter of was
est. is the abbreviation for established
RA is the Royal Artillery, whose soldiers are gunners

explanation.surface: Arsenal, the Gunners, set up a training ground in China.
explanation.walkthrough: China and Gunners suggest Arsenal football club's overseas academy; China is cockney rhyming slang and Gunners the Royal Artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: A palaestra was the wrestling school or exercise ground of ancient Greece, a place for athletic training.

definitions.note: used as an adjective, below the sea

indicators.note: storms throw things about violently, so these letters are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: used as written
used as written

explanation.surface: A submarine crew rides out storms at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Submarine looks like the vessel, a noun; it is the adjective meaning under the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Submarine as an adjective means existing or happening beneath the surface of the sea.

clue.text: Noisy sleeper more upset about onset of nightmares

indicators.note: the onset is the beginning, so only the first letter of the next word is used
about means around, so one piece goes outside the other

blocks.note: sorer means more upset or aggrieved
the first letter of nightmares

explanation.surface: A restless sleeper grows more distressed as nightmares begin.
explanation.walkthrough: Upset looks like an anagram signal; 'more upset' is just a comparative adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who snores makes a rasping noise while asleep, so a snorer is a noisy sleeper.

clue.text: Relative bitten by bug, causing laughter

indicators.note: something bitten is held between the jaws, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: to bug someone is to annoy or rile them
sib is short for sibling, a relative

explanation.surface: A relative gets bitten by an insect, which everyone finds hilarious.
explanation.walkthrough: Bug looks like an insect; it is the verb meaning annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Risible means laughable, provoking laughter, often with ridicule.

clue.text: Some marital infidelity is remedy for restlessness

indicators.note: some means a portion of the words that follow, so the letters lie inside them

blocks.note: a run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Cheating on a spouse is offered as a cure for being restless.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritalin is a brand of methylphenidate, prescribed for hyperactivity and attention disorders.

clue.text: Endings of Goldfinger and The Servant reportedly filmed again

indicators.note: endings means the final letters of the words that follow are taken
reportedly means as it is said, so the word is replaced by one that is pronounced the same

blocks.note: the last letters of Goldfinger and The; 'and' just links them
a maid is a servant

explanation.surface: Goldfinger and The Servant are 1960s films that were later remade.
explanation.walkthrough: The Servant (1963) and Goldfinger (1964) look like a pair of titles, but The is split off and Servant stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A film that has been remade has been shot again as a new version.

clue.text: Writer stays married, in the same place

blocks.note: the setter, as writer of the clue, refers to themselves as I
to bide is to stay or remain
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: An author remains married and lives in the same house.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibidem is the Latin footnote term meaning in the same source, literally in the same place.

indicators.note: acting misguidedly means going the wrong way, so these letters end up out of order

blocks.note: used as written

explanation.surface: A government taxes baby boomers, wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: Taxing looks like a tax policy; it means demanding or irksome.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taxing makes heavy demands and wears you out, so it is troublesome or annoying.

clue.text: Goes off to support Tooting's foremost revolutionaries

indicators.note: foremost means at the very front, so only the first letter is taken
in a down answer a support sits underneath, so this piece comes below the other

blocks.note: the first letter of Tooting
food that goes off rots

explanation.surface: Revolutionaries go off to back the leading figures in Tooting.
explanation.walkthrough: Tooting is a district of south London, long associated with left-wing politics through 'Citizen Smith'.
explanation.definitionFit: Trots is a colloquial, often dismissive, name for Trotskyists, far-left revolutionaries.

clue.text: Read out part of rosary for venerable saint

indicators.note: read out means spoken aloud, so the word is swapped for one sounding identical

blocks.note: a rosary is a string of beads

explanation.surface: Someone reads out a portion of the rosary for a holy saint.
explanation.walkthrough: The Venerable Bede was the 8th-century Northumbrian monk and historian; venerable is part of his customary title.
explanation.definitionFit: Bede is the English saint always styled the Venerable Bede, so the description identifies him.

indicators.note: intermittently means at intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of hit outlaw

explanation.surface: Someone occasionally strikes an outlaw during a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrap looks like a fight, fitting the outlaw scene; it is a tiny bit.
explanation.definitionFit: An iota, the smallest Greek letter, means a very small amount, a scrap or jot.

indicators.note: short means cut down, so the word loses its last letter
in means placed inside, so the first piece goes within the second

blocks.note: dim means dark or poorly lit
hot means sexy

explanation.surface: Someone looks sexy wearing a short, dark loincloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is the length of cloth worn by Indian men, wrapped round the waist and legs like a loincloth.

blocks.note: poor means bad, of low quality
kisser is slang for mouth

explanation.surface: Someone disparages people who are bad at kissing.
explanation.walkthrough: To slag off is British slang for criticising someone harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: To badmouth someone is to criticise them maliciously, the same as slagging them off.

indicators.note: backed means moved backwards, so the name is read from end to start

blocks.note: a film is a thin layer, like a mist on glass
Demi Moore is the American film actress

explanation.surface: An actress backed a film that came out at a bad time.
explanation.walkthrough: Film looks like a movie, matching Ms Moore; it is a thin haze.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mistimed is done at the wrong moment, which is what inopportune means.

clue.text: Runs out of wine and curry

indicators.note: out of means removed from, so the letter for runs is taken away from the wine

blocks.note: R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs
Marsala is a fortified wine from Sicily

explanation.surface: A dinner party runs out of wine and curry.
explanation.walkthrough: Runs out of looks like a supply running dry, but runs is the letter and out of the removal.
explanation.definitionFit: A masala is a spiced South Asian dish, so it is a type of curry.
